  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The issue-mode cleanup timing instructions conflict, leaving an unattended resume without a reliable operational trigger to archive the stopped session.
  WHY: The Step 0 and Step 1 instructions and cleanup header give contradictory timing, so a session following the steps literally may attempt cleanup before the `Source issue:` identifier is available or defer cleanup without running it.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:191-192 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Skipping cleanup when the `Source issue:` line is missing is silent and not reported.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a project-mode resume with no zombie checkers from an issue-mode resume where cleanup was skipped because the header was missing.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md:12, 190-192 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: Cleanup failures from a transient title-rename or issue-label read error have no clearly surfaced failure path.
  WHY: A rename failure can leave the session with a title cleanup will not match, and a label-read failure can leave the stopped session visible without a durable error marker while archival is skipped.
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py:262-263 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The contract test checks the rename-failure fallback string but does not assert the preceding instruction to retry the rename once.
  WHY: A future edit could remove the retry instruction while the test still passes, weakening recovery from a transient rename failure.

- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Step 0 child bullet (lines 12-14) and Step 1 "Resolve the plan doc." (line 18) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Contradictory placement of the issue-mode cleanup trigger.
  WHY: The Step 0 bullet introduces the cleanup trigger as a child of the Session preflight (Step 0), but the text defers it to Step 1. An unattended session following the step-by-step flow may attempt cleanup in Step 0 (before the `Source issue:` identifier is read), resulting in a no-op or failure, or defer it without a clear mechanism to revisit it, leaving the stopped session unarchived.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Zombie-checker cleanup header (line 187) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The header states "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene", which contradicts the instruction that issue-mode cleanup runs at the end of Step 1.
  WHY: An unattended session reading the header may incorrectly attempt the cleanup in Step 0, before the necessary `Source issue:` identifier is available from the plan read in Step 1.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Zombie-checker cleanup section (lines 191-192) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Cleanup skip (when `Source issue:` line is missing) is silent and not logged/reported.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish between a project-mode resume that has no zombie checkers and an issue-mode resume where the cleanup was silently dropped due to a missing header, making the operator-visible report indistinguishable.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Zombie-checker cleanup logic (lines 190-192) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Transient errors in `set_session_title` (rename) or `mcp__github__issue_read` (label read) have no documented failure-handling path.
  WHY: Rename failures can leave the session with its old title (which cleanup won't match), and label-read failures can skip archival without surfacing an error, requiring manual operator intervention.
